note.subject: geography
note.why_in_news: The Government of India formally identified 28 strategic places and geographical features on the official Survey of India map to ensure accurate recognition of territory.
note.fact_box: On October 2, 2026, the Government of India and the Union Territory of Ladakh administration finalized the inclusion of 28 features. These include peaks like Zorawar Peak and Kanishka Peak, and glaciers like Parpik and Skamri.

prelims_pointers.text: Zorawar Peak and Kanishka Peak are strategic geographical features in the Ladakh region.
The Survey of India (SoI) is the national survey and mapping agency of India.
A total of 28 strategic places and geographical features were identified on October 2, 2026.

note.mains_question: Discuss the significance of accurate cartographic representation in safeguarding India's territorial integrity and managing border security in high-altitude regions.

note.subject: economy
note.why_in_news: The introduction of the CURE Act 2026 replaces the GHMC Act 1955, shifting property tax to a Capital Value System and altering local governance in Hyderabad's urban regions.
note.fact_box: The Core Urban Region (Integrated Governance) Act, 2026 (CURE Act) replaces the GHMC Act, 1955. It governs the GHMC, Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation, and Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC). The new legislation shifts property tax calculation to a Capital Value System.

prelims_pointers.text: CURE Act: Core Urban Region (Integrated Governance) Act, 2026
The CURE Act replaces the GHMC Act, 1955 for Hyderabad's municipal governance
Capital Value System: A property tax model based on the market value of the property rather than annual rental value

note.mains_question: Discuss the implications of shifting to a Capital Value System for property taxation on urban infrastructure development and municipal fiscal autonomy.
note.title: CURE Act shifts property tax to Capital Value System, potentially doubling CMC taxes

note.subject: social_justice
note.why_in_news: Tamil Nadu CM launched the ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme to provide free bus travel for women and transgender persons across seven State Transport Corporations.
note.fact_box: The scheme was launched on October 2, 2026, at Koyambedu bus terminus, Chennai. It covers 12,695 buses and aims to benefit 84.32 lakh women and transgender persons daily. The scheme excludes Chengalpattu and Tiruppur districts.

prelims_pointers.text: Vettri Payanam: Tamil Nadu state government scheme providing free bus travel for women and transgender persons.
The scheme covers 12,695 buses across seven State Transport Corporations in Tamil Nadu.
The scheme targets a daily benefit for 84.32 lakh individuals.
Koyambedu: Major bus terminus in Chennai, Tamil Nadu.

note.mains_question: Discuss how targeted social welfare schemes like free public transport can facilitate gender equality and economic inclusion for marginalized communities in India.

note.subject: history_culture
note.why_in_news: The Madras High Court directed the Tamil Nadu government to submit a status report on removing caste-based names from public roads and streets.
note.fact_box: The order was issued by the First Division Bench of the Madras High Court on October 1, 2026. It references a 1978 Government Order and a Sendhamangalam police FIR regarding the removal of caste appellations from public infrastructure.

prelims_pointers.text: Madras High Court: Located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu
The court mandated a status report submission within four weeks of the October 1, 2026 order
The judicial scrutiny refers back to a 1978 Government Order regarding caste appellations

note.mains_question: Discuss the constitutional implications of caste-based nomenclature in public infrastructure and its impact on the principle of equality and social dignity.
